State that INFERENCE_API_KEY must stay server-only and must never be exposed in client bundles.

content.value_statement: Teams need agent chat UIs without building streaming, tools, and approvals from scratch. This skill explains how to add the inference.sh Agent component to React or Next.js.
actual_capabilities: Shows the shadcn command for adding the inference.sh Agent component.
Documents a Next.js API proxy route using @inferencesh/sdk.
Shows INFERENCE_API_KEY setup for local server configuration.
Demonstrates rendering an Agent component with proxyUrl and agentConfig.
Documents scoped client-side tools for browser form interaction.
Lists Agent props for files, images, name, config, and proxyUrl.
limitations: Requires an inference.sh API key and service access.
Targets React and Next.js projects, not other front-end frameworks.
Depends on remote registry and package availability.
Provides documentation only; it does not include component source files.

use_cases.title: Add an Agent Chat Page
use_cases.description: Create a Next.js page that renders an Agent component with streaming and a proxy route.

use_cases.title: Prototype a SaaS Copilot
use_cases.description: Test a copilot interface that supports approvals, file inputs, images, and tool status updates.

use_cases.title: Connect Browser Tools
use_cases.description: Wire scoped client-side tools so an assistant can inspect and fill page forms with review controls.

prompt_templates.title: Install the Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup in a new project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-ui to help me add the inference.sh Agent component to my Next.js app. Include the install steps, proxy route, and environment variable checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Render a Basic Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-ui to design a simple React page with the Agent component. Explain the required props and where the proxy URL should point.

prompt_templates.title: Add Client Tools
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-ui to plan a client-side tools setup for a form assistant. Include how scoped tools should be connected and reviewed by users.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-ui to audit my planned Agent integration for production. Focus on API key handling, remote installs, uploads, approvals, and user confirmation flows.

output_examples.input: I need an agent page in a Next.js dashboard.
output_examples.output: A concise setup plan covering the component install, server proxy route, API key placement, and minimal page structure.

output_examples.input: I want the assistant to help fill a customer intake form.
output_examples.output: A workflow description for scoped browser tools, visible approvals, and user confirmation before any form changes are submitted.

output_examples.input: Check whether my Agent integration is ready for production.
output_examples.output: A review checklist covering remote dependency review, upload limits, server-only secrets, approval behavior, and fallback handling.

best_practices: Keep API keys in server-only environment files and never expose them to client bundles.
Review remote component changes before adding them to production projects.
Use approval flows for tools that change forms, files, or account data.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real API keys into chat prompts or shared issue threads.
Do not enable file or image uploads without validating size, type, and access scope.
Do not let client-side tools submit sensitive forms without user confirmation.

faq.question: What frameworks does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets React and Next.js applications that can use the shadcn component workflow.

faq.question: Does it include the Agent component source?
faq.answer: No. The skill documents how to add the component from the inference.sh registry.

faq.question: Does it require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented proxy route expects an INFERENCE_API_KEY stored in a server-only environment file.

faq.question: Can the agent use browser tools?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill shows scoped client-side tools that can inspect and fill forms in the browser.

faq.question: Does it support human approval flows?
faq.answer: Yes. The feature list describes built-in approval states for tool lifecycle workflows.

faq.question: Should I review the remote install before production?
faq.answer: Yes. Review generated files, package versions, and registry content before using it in production.
